blockers.description: Phase 0 was planned around public documentation even though SiriusXM intentionally publishes no third-party authentication contract; its NO-GO conclusion does not answer the project question.
blockers.workaround: Supersede the old evidence premise with the completed owner-authorized empirical capture and a real WKWebView proof.

blockers.description: Chromium login plus native token replay proves session portability but does not prove SiriusXM accepts the actual macOS WKWebView runtime.
blockers.workaround: Build a disposable WKWebView POC and ask the account owner to complete the login manually when it is ready.

human_actions_pending.action: Complete two manual SiriusXM logins inside the disposable native WKWebView POC when prompted.
human_actions_pending.context: The account owner must operate authentication; automation must not enter credentials, handle challenges, or evade bot controls.

decisions.decision: The prior Phase 0 NO-GO is superseded and must not gate the project.
decisions.rationale: It was derived from an incorrect public-documentation-only premise and never tested the intended owner-operated browser or native flows.

decisions.decision: Prefer a purpose-scoped WKWebView login followed by native URLSession requests if the real WKWebView proof succeeds.
decisions.rationale: The browser-issued session is portable to an honest native client, and this path avoids exposing the subscriber password to Sirius Mac.

decisions.decision: Use native-direct password authentication only if the real WKWebView flow is unsupported.
decisions.rationale: Direct authentication is empirically viable, but the project will implement only one sign-in path and should minimize credential handling.

decisions.decision: Retain only sanitized protocol metadata; never persist raw HAR, cookies, tokens, authorization headers, response bodies, stream URLs, playback keys, or credentials.
decisions.rationale: The capture contains reusable account secrets and is unnecessary after the protocol shape is understood.

context_notes: Empirical findings: POST device/v2/devices; POST session/v1/sessions/anonymous; GET identity/v1/identities/status; POST identity/v1/identities/authenticate/password with handle/password; POST session/v1/sessions/authenticated; Bearer-authenticated account/profile/subscription APIs; POST playback/play/v1/tuneSource; Bearer-authenticated playback key retrieval. A captured authenticated access token returned HTTP 200 from a standalone native-style request using an honest SiriusMacAuthPOC user agent, and native tuneSource, master manifest, child manifest, and key-document retrieval succeeded. SiriusXM stores AUTH_TOKEN, DEVICE_GRANT, and LOGICAL_CLOCK as first-party JavaScript-readable cookies, making WKHTTPCookieStore handoff plausible. Unknowns: actual WKWebView compatibility, session refresh-token mechanics, and AVFoundation handling of the authenticated AES-128 key URI. The dedicated browser was closed and every /private/tmp/sxm-* raw artifact was deleted.
